cards.anchor: The valued outcome is three elevation-vial attenuations with normalized spread at most 4 percent at second 120, reducing stirring time if feasible. One stipulated 300 rpm trial stopped at second 60 and yielded 0.204, 0.209 and 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread. This challenges universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm but does not establish repeatable sufficiency or timer-controlled 900 rpm success.
cards.burden: Six fresh trials consume the full 90-minute session allowance. Manual five-second image entries, raw sample measurements and paired order records are required. Treat unavailable bubble identification and absolute concentration calibration as outside the claim; neither is indispensable to the bounded duration-versus-vial comparison.
cards.construction: Hypothetical construction: run three fresh paired comparisons at commanded 900 rpm, alternating which arm runs first across pairs. In the timer arm stop exactly at second 60, record the preferred rule in shadow mode and never restart. In the enabled arm use three successive five-second side spreads at most 4 percent as the stop rule, with a hard stop at second 105. Each trial uses 150 mL tap water and 0.30 mL dye in the rinsed 250 mL beaker, fixed addition location, one dye bottle, common references and locked camera settings. Use the spill tray and stop on liquid escape. Sample 1 mL from each of 10, 28 and 45 mm within ten seconds after second 120, alternating depth order within pairs. Record cessation times, all raw readings and target failures.
cards.defeat: Repeated timer-arm vial spreads above 4 percent while longer enabled arms meet the target defeats the proposed dispensability of additional agitation in this comparison. If both fail, reject the construction as an adequate recipe and leave the causal accounts unresolved. If enabled arms stop at or before 60, there is no demonstrated timer saving or post-60 extension to explain. A lower side spread or fewer specks without successful final vials cannot rescue the card.
cards.mutation: Hypothesis: replace optical permission to continue stirring with a fixed timer while retaining the optical rule as a recorded observer. This separates an outcome test from the controller that may prolong agitation in response to its own optical disturbances.
cards.prediction_candidate: Hypothesis prediction: across pairs with actual enabled-arm stirring beyond 60 seconds, timer and enabled arms both attain final-vial spread at most 4 percent, although the timer shadow rule can still fail at cessation. The timer then uses fewer stirring seconds. This would support dispensability of observed extensions under these conditions; it would not prove the disturbance-renewal mechanism or identify specks.
cards.prediction_rival: Rival prediction: the timer arm retains final-vial spread above 4 percent while additional enabled-arm stirring brings spread to at most 4 percent. Consistent paired outcomes would favor useful extra redistribution under this recipe, without establishing necessity of 900 rpm or of this particular optical rule.
cards.probe: Compare paired final-vial spreads and stirring seconds; record the enabled rule decisions and timer shadow decisions, side attenuations every five seconds, surface depression and speck-containing frames before and after cessation. The control contrast exists wherever enabled commands differ from the fixed timer, especially beyond second 60. Require final-vial success in both arms plus actual longer enabled duration before interpreting a pair as unnecessary extension. Image changes after stop supply temporal evidence only and cannot alone establish uniformity or a causal feedback loop.
cards.rival: Hypothesis: real dye gradients cause optical spread, and the rule requests additional agitation that materially improves the final sampled outcome.
unknowns: Matched 900 rpm final-vial readings and actual preferred-rule stopping duration are absent; every proposed paired result remains a hypothesis.
The timer and enabled arms can have different quiet durations before second 120. Record those durations; final differences cannot be attributed solely to extra stirring.
Specks may be bubbles, reflections or undissolved dye; the specific agitation-to-disturbance return mechanism is unverified.
Sampling can disturb gradients, commanded speed lacks independent verification, and common-aliquot repeatability does not calibrate concentration.

Three pairs limit replication and leave order effects possible. Other solutes, viscosities, vessel sizes and continuous processes are untested; the synthetic proxy establishes no real chemical or human benefit.
